title: Orsen and the Choir
premise: Marguerite Dravenmoor, a memory-thief who trades in stolen recollections along the smuggler roads of the Thornfell mountains, finds a starving boy on his doorstep speaking a language older than any kingdom. The child carries a song — the last verse of the Choir, an ancient collective consciousness that once held the usurper's bloodline in check — and both the usurper's inquisitors and the free cities' spymasters will kill to control it. Marguerite, who has never kept anything he couldn't sell, must choose between selling the boy's secret and becoming the family he never believed he deserved. In the end, Marguerite gives up his own stolen hoard of memories to complete the Choir's song, shattering the usurper's claim of legitimacy before her armies reach the free cities — at the cost of forgetting the boy entirely, until the Choir itself returns what was freely given.
about_author: Mara Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from mountain villages before turning to fiction. She writes about memory, borders, and the families people build when their bloodlines fail them.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Sang Before Names
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine job stealing a merchant's grief goes wrong when Marguerite returns home to find a mute, starving boy on his doorstep, humming a melody that makes his stolen memories stir unbidden. Emotional beat: wary curiosity cracking open a loner's armor.

chapters.title: What the Thornfell Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Seeking a buyer for the boy's strange language, Marguerite consults a blind fence who recognizes the tongue as pre-kingdom Choir-speech — and warns that the usurper's inquisitors pay in gold for its speakers, dead or alive. Beat: dread replacing greed.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sister Veyra's POV, the usurper's chief inquisitor, tracking a 'choral anomaly' into the mountains. She burns a village that sheltered the boy, revealing the regime's terror with cold bureaucratic calm. Beat: chilling escalation; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road South
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Fleeing toward the free city of Cael Harrow, Marguerite teaches the boy — named Orsen by a wayhouse keeper — to survive the roads, and Orsen begins singing fragments that return Marguerite memories he'd sold years ago. Beat: tentative found-family tenderness.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Song
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, rendered in his emerging grasp of language. He reveals he fled a massacre of the last Choir-keepers and that the song chooses carriers, not owners. Marguerite realizes his own mother was a Keeper. Beat: identity upheaval; love against duty takes root.

chapters.title: The Free City's Price
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In Cael Harrow, spymaster Odile Corvane offers protection for Orsen — if Marguerite steals the usurper's legitimacy-charter from her fortress-vault. Marguerite accepts, hiding that the Choir needs the charter as a resonant vessel. Beat: bargain struck, trap half-seen.

chapters.title: Vault of Hollow Kings
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The heist through the usurper's vault succeeds until Veyra corners him; Orsen, defying orders, sings the fortress wards awake, and the two escape as the usurper learns the Choir lives. Beat: triumph curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Where Loyalties Fray
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile plans to weaponize Orsen rather than free him; Marguerite discovers the betrayal just as the usurper's armies march. Torn between the free cities' survival and the boy's freedom, Marguerite flees with Orsen into the high passes. Beat: heartbreak and resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs at the Choir's ruined mountain sanctuary. To finish the song before Veyra's forces arrive, the Choir demands a carrier surrender all their memories. Marguerite volunteers his hoard — every theft, every sale, every lonely year. Beat: sacrificial climax; justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Choir of the Unforgotten
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, then Marguerite's. The completed song unmakes the usurper's blood-oath before her armies; Veyra, hearing it, lays down her ledger. Memory-less Marguerite wakes to a stranger-child calling him family — and the Choir, merciful, returns one memory: Orsen's face at the door. Beat: bittersweet resolution; found family sealed.
